Class Hdf5CompoundIO

java.lang.Object
global.thalion.ttio.hdf5.Hdf5CompoundIO
public final class Hdf5CompoundIO extends Object
Write/read helper for the fixed compound metadata datasets described in format-spec section 6. Supports variable-length fields (VL_STRING and VL_BYTES) in writes via a split-write strategy compatible with HDF5 1.14 Java bindings.

HDF5 1.14 compatibility note: The HDF5 1.14 JNI wrapper for H5Dwrite and H5DwriteVL calls h5str_detect_vlen on the memory type before every write, and if any H5T_VLEN field is present it routes through translate_wbuf / translate_rbuf, which calls GetObjectArrayElement on a jbyteArray -- undefined behaviour that causes a JVM SIGSEGV.

When a schema contains any VL field (VL_STRING or VL_BYTES), the write path splits:

  1. Create the dataset with the full compound file type.
  2. Write only the non-VL (primitive) fields via H5Dwrite(byte[]) with a projection memory type that excludes all VL fields.
  3. Write each VL_STRING column via H5.H5Dwrite_VLStrings(long,long,long,long,long,Object[]).
  4. Write each VL_BYTES column via the VlBytesFFM helper, which uses the Java 21 Foreign Function & Memory (FFM) API to call the native C H5Dwrite directly, bypassing the JNI translate_wbuf path entirely.
For schemas with no VL fields at all, the original full-compound byte-buffer approach is used unchanged (compatible with HDF5 1.14).

The read path applies the same split strategy when any VL field is present.

    • writeCompoundDataset

      public static void writeCompoundDataset(Hdf5Group parent, String datasetName, Hdf5CompoundIO.Schema schema, int count, Hdf5CompoundIO.RowPacker packer)
      Write a compound dataset. For schemas with any VL field (VL_STRING or VL_BYTES), uses a split strategy to avoid the HDF5 1.14 crash. For schemas without any VL fields, uses the original full-compound byte-buffer approach.

    • readCompoundPrimitives

      public static List<Object[]> readCompoundPrimitives(Hdf5Group parent, String datasetName, Hdf5CompoundIO.Schema schema)
      Read a compound dataset returning only the primitive (non-VL) fields. VL_STRING fields are returned as empty strings and VL_BYTES fields as empty byte arrays. Use readCompoundFull(Hdf5Group, String, Hdf5CompoundIO.Schema) to also decode the VL fields.
      Parameters:
      parent - the group that owns the dataset
      datasetName - the dataset name inside parent
      schema - the full schema describing the on-disk layout
      Returns:
      one Object[] per record, in field order; an empty list if the dataset is missing or empty

    • readCompoundFull

      public static List<Object[]> readCompoundFull(Hdf5Group parent, String datasetName, Hdf5CompoundIO.Schema schema)
      Read a compound dataset returning all fields. Uses a split-read strategy for HDF5 1.14 compatibility when any VL field (VL_STRING or VL_BYTES) is present:
      1. Read primitive (non-VL) fields via H5Dread(byte[]) with a projection memory type that excludes all VL fields.
      2. Read each VL_STRING column via H5.H5Dread_VLStrings(long,long,long,long,long,Object[]).
      3. Read each VL_BYTES column via the FFM helper VlBytesFFM.read(long, long, long, int) which calls the native C H5Dread directly, bypassing the JNI translate_rbuf interception entirely.
      When no VL fields are present, uses the original full-compound byte-buffer approach.
